fields.description:
Delete the two bridge verbs that are dead on arrival: `rebar bridge-status` and `rebar purge-bridge`.

This is pure dead-code deletion. It is carved out of `4752-3afb-e8bd-448a` ("Establish the `bridge`
verb group") so it can land immediately, with NO dependency on any sibling — nothing in the new
`bridge` surface replaces either verb, so nothing has to ship first.

## Why each verb is dead

**`bridge-status`** — its producer has never existed in this repo. The reader consumes
`<tracker>/.bridge-status.json`, but rebar was extracted from digital-service-orchestra on
2026-06-08 and the reader was a knowing tombstone from day one; on every post-cutover repo it exits
1 ("No bridge status file found"). Verified: zero references to the producer in `docs/`, `scripts/`
or `.github/`. Note also that the citation in its module docstring — "epic 3a03" — is DANGLING: in
this repo `3a03` resolves to an unrelated test-isolation bug created 11 days AFTER the comment
citing it. The real epic is `3006-e198-13db-4e1f`. That dangling citation dies with the module, so
the "correct the 3a03 citation" obligation from `4752` is discharged here for this file.

**`purge-bridge`** — five commits, every one an automated lint sweep or safety retrofit, none a
feature or a bug fix, and no script, workflow, or runbook invokes it. Its `--keep` flag is also
inverted-sense (it deletes everything NOT matching), which is exactly the kind of surface the
bridge redesign is removing rather than renaming.

## User-facing strings retire WITH the verbs (carried from `4752` section B6)

Retiring `bridge-status` leaves two strings pointing at a verb that no longer exists:
* `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge.py:32` — `_USAGE = "Usage: ticket bridge-status [--output json]"`
  (that module IS the `bridge-status` implementation, so it retires whole, `_USAGE` included);
* `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_status.schema.json:5`, whose description names
  `rebar bridge-status --output json`. The schema file is retired outright, since sibling
  `b69c-5787-81b8-4052` builds `bridge status` on durable state and publishes its own schema.

`purge-bridge` likewise carries `src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py:37`
(`_USAGE = "Usage: ticket-purge-bridge.sh --keep=<PROJECT_KEY> [--dry-run]"` — itself a stale
reference to a bash script deleted at the Tier-E cutover) and `src/rebar/_cli/help/purge-bridge.txt`.

## Enumerated consumers (all deletions or edits, no migrations)

CLI wiring: `src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py` — the `_BRIDGE` frozenset at line 121 (drop
`bridge-status` and `purge-bridge`, keep `bridge-fsck`), the `bridge-status` arm at ~305 and the
`purge-bridge` arm at ~312.
Help: `src/rebar/_cli/help/overview.txt` (lines naming both verbs),
`src/rebar/_cli/help/bridge-status.txt`, `src/rebar/_cli/help/purge-bridge.txt`.
Implementation: `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge.py`, `src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py`.
Schemas: `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_status.schema.json`.
Tests (delete, they only cover the retired verbs): `tests/scripts/bridge/test_bridge_status.py`,
`tests/unit/test_purge_bridge_locked_commit.py`,
`tests/interfaces/store/test_purge_bridge_prune_concurrency.py`,
`tests/interfaces/store/_purge_race_worker.py`.
Contract tests (edit): `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_coverage.py` — the
`"bridge-status": EXEMPT_BRIDGE` entry at ~125 goes away with the schema;
`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_help_overview_coverage.py` — the verb inventory.
Docs: `docs/cli-reference.md` (the `### purge-bridge` section at ~324 and the `bridge-status`
entry), `docs/exit-codes.md` (rows at 79 and 101).

Additional consumers:

- `src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py`: remove the `BRIDGE_STATUS` export, constant, and
  `OUTPUT_SCHEMAS["bridge_status"]` entry together with `bridge_status.schema.json`.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads_cli.py`: replace both live
  `Run: ticket bridge-status for details.` warnings with neutral guidance to inspect unresolved
  bridge alerts. Do not point at `bridge status`, because that sibling command has not landed yet.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/output.py`: remove `bridge-status` from the report-profile
  documentation.
- `docs/output-schemas.md`: remove the `bridge-status` to `bridge_status` row.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: add release notes for both retirements; existing historical entries remain
  intentionally.

## Verification oracle

The B6 oracle is exact: a behavioral contract test proves both retired CLI tokens are unknown and
absent from top-level help, then asserts zero `bridge-status` or `purge-bridge` matches in the
shipped package tree `src/rebar` and the active command-contract docs `docs/cli-reference.md`,
`docs/exit-codes.md`, and `docs/output-schemas.md`. Tests, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/archive` are
excluded because they intentionally retain specification or historical evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge-status` exits as an unknown command.
- [ ] `rebar purge-bridge` exits as an unknown command.
- [ ] Neither retired command appears in `rebar --help`.
- [ ] `src/rebar/_engine_support/bridge.py` and `src/rebar/_commands/purge_bridge.py` are deleted,
      not shimmed; no alias or deprecation forwarder ships for either verb.
- [ ] `src/rebar/schemas/bridge_status.schema.json` is deleted and the schema-coverage contract test
      passes without a `bridge-status` exemption entry.
- [ ] The schema registry has no `BRIDGE_STATUS` export, constant, or output-schema entry.
- [ ] Both surviving read warnings provide neutral bridge-alert guidance and name no retired or
      not-yet-shipped command.
- [ ] The shipped-package and active-doc zero-match oracle passes, covering `_USAGE` strings,
      `help/*.txt`, `overview.txt`, and active command-contract docs.
- [ ] The tests that exist ONLY to cover the retired verbs are deleted in the same change; the full
      suite is green with no skips or xfails left behind.
- [ ] `docs/cli-reference.md`, `docs/exit-codes.md`, and `docs/output-schemas.md` no longer list
      either verb or its retired output schema.
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` records both retirements.
- [ ] The dangling "epic 3a03" citation in `_engine_support/bridge.py`'s docstring is gone (it dies
      with the module); a grep confirms no surviving reference in the bridge code path cites `3a03`.
- [ ] No behaviour of any SURVIVING verb changes: `bridge-fsck` still dispatches through the
      trimmed `_BRIDGE` set, and the existing top-level `rebar doctor` store link-repair command is
      untouched.
